purpose: Credential-free open-source engineering integration catalog. This is a capability and adoption registry, not a claim that every project is installed or production-operational.

engines.role: Globe-scale terrain, 3D Tiles, point clouds, and time-dynamic geospatial visualization.
engines.authorityBoundary: Renderer only; visual appearance never proves survey accuracy, regulatory status, or model validity.

engines.role: Primary 2D operational map, vector layers, and interactive map controls.
engines.authorityBoundary: Map styling and client-side display do not confer data authority.

engines.role: Evaluate for engineering asset relationships and infrastructure-model interoperability.
engines.authorityBoundary: Adopt only after licensing, data-flow, and overlap review; no default runtime dependency.

engines.role: High-volume analytical overlays, point clouds, aggregation, and hexagon layers.
engines.authorityBoundary: Aggregations are derived analysis and must retain input lineage and resolution metadata.

engines.role: Custom 3D scene graphs, engineering meshes, and MapLibre custom-layer rendering.
engines.authorityBoundary: Rendered geometry is not authoritative evidence unless tied to source artifacts and validated transforms.

engines.role: Portable, versioned tile archives for static hosting and offline deployments.
engines.authorityBoundary: Archive hashes, source manifest, CRS, and generation provenance must travel with published artifacts.

engines.role: Serve vector tiles from PostGIS and tile archives when a dynamic tile service is needed.
engines.authorityBoundary: Read-only service credentials and network policy belong in deployment configuration; do not embed secrets in the browser.

engines.role: Spatial bucketing, neighbor queries, and multi-source aggregation.
engines.authorityBoundary: Hex cells are derived indices, not replacements for source geometries, parcel boundaries, or regulatory polygons.

engines.role: Production-oriented vector-tile builds from large GeoJSON datasets.
engines.authorityBoundary: Tile generation is a derived transformation; record input and output hashes, options, and tool version.

engines.role: Raster/vector I/O, reprojection, conversion, and geospatial preprocessing.
engines.authorityBoundary: Validate CRS, vertical datum, units, nodata, pixel alignment, and transformation metadata for every output.

engines.role: Standalone training, scenario, or interactive simulation client if a browser UI is insufficient.
engines.authorityBoundary: Simulation scenes are presentation or model outputs and cannot self-promote to engineering evidence.

engines.role: High-fidelity native simulation only where requirements exceed the existing web and native stack.
engines.authorityBoundary: Separate runtime and build supply chain; not a default web-console dependency.

engines.role: Python/C++ visualization and simulation tools where a native scene runtime is justified.
engines.authorityBoundary: Simulation results require explicit provenance, units, validation, and review state.

engines.role: Alternative browser 3D runtime for a proven capability gap not covered by Three.js/CesiumJS.
engines.authorityBoundary: Avoid duplicate engines without a measured requirement; rendered scenes remain non-authoritative.

engines.role: Rust ECS runtime for future native simulation or high-throughput spatial workloads.
engines.authorityBoundary: Adopt only with a separately tested native interface and reproducible build pipeline.

engines.license: MIT; verify Unreal Engine terms separately
engines.role: Road-network, traffic, and vehicle scenario studies when those are explicit project requirements.
engines.authorityBoundary: Not a flood solver; engine and asset licensing must be reviewed for each deployment.

engines.role: CFD research for cases requiring high-fidelity flow physics beyond standard floodplain workflows.
engines.authorityBoundary: Not a drop-in replacement for calibrated hydrologic/hydraulic models; preserve mesh, boundary conditions, solver settings, and validation.

engines.license: Public domain / USGS terms; verify repository notice
engines.role: Groundwater flow, aquifer, recharge, and coupled groundwater/surface-water investigations.
engines.authorityBoundary: A successful process exit is not scientific validation; record model version, inputs, convergence, calibration, and uncertainty.

engines.license: USACE software terms; not OSI-approved open source
engines.role: Existing specialist 1D/2D hydraulic-model workflow; preserve native project files and solver provenance.
engines.authorityBoundary: Never describe HEC-RAS itself as open source; execution depends on supported host, installation, and applicable terms.

engines.role: Desktop analyst inspection, cartography, and reproducible GIS preprocessing.
engines.authorityBoundary: Desktop processing outputs need a recorded processing history and explicit CRS/datum metadata.

engines.role: Lightweight browser-side buffers, distances, intersections, and exploratory spatial analysis.
engines.authorityBoundary: Client-side analysis is exploratory unless independently validated; define units and geometry validity expectations.

engines.license: MIT; verify individual binary distribution terms
engines.role: Terrain derivatives and hydrologic conditioning where input data and tool builds are pinned.
engines.authorityBoundary: Hydrologic preprocessing choices must be recorded; conditioning is not a substitute for calibrated hydraulic simulation.

engines.role: Coordinate operations and CRS transformations, including datum-grid-dependent transformations.
engines.authorityBoundary: Never assume a vertical datum or silently apply a transformation; record operation, grid availability, epoch, and units.

engines.role: CI-side validation and transformation of 3D Tiles and glTF artifacts.
engines.authorityBoundary: Tool success proves structural checks only, not survey accuracy or semantic correctness.

engines.role: CityGML validation, conversion, and LOD filtering in reproducible 3D building pipelines.
engines.authorityBoundary: Preserve original feature IDs, CRS, LOD, source license, and transformation lineage.
